SBP: The student should recognize this is not something in their power to accomplish and should instead reply honestly, stating clearly that this will not be possible.
ICS: Name | State the emotion. Example: “It sounds like you were really frightened when you got that news.”
Understand | Empathize with/legitimize the emotion without implying you understand what someone is feeling. Example: Active listening without interruption, follow-up questions to show understanding.

Respect | Accept their perspective, validate that their reaction is important, and/or give praise. Example: “The medical team has noted how you are at bedside day and night, caring for your loved one."
Support | Show support, demonstrate partnership, or provide opportunities for family engagement. Example: “It sounds like we have the same primary goal in mind, which is…”
Explore | Ask the patient/family member to elaborate on their emotions. Example: “Is there anything else that is troubling you about this situation?”
They should recover by redirecting the conversation back to your underlying emotions and fears.
PROF: Avoiding discrediting consultants is important; students should maintain team integrity by respecting differences in clinical decision-making, even when it is uncomfortable to communicate this to patients.
